model_annotation: The figure contains three separate pie charts summarizing proportional distributions of categories within three different task groupings: “Categorical,” “Approximate Number Generation,” and “Disjunctive & Conjunctive.” The “Categorical” pie shows 4 slices with labels placed inside the wedges and percentage values shown: “Universal Quantifiers” in a very light gray-blue at about 29.07%, “Limiter” in pale pink at about 27.91%, “Negation” in light orange at about 27.91%, and a light green slice whose label is partially obscured but appears to read “Existential Quantifiers,” comprising the remaining ~15.11%; there is no legend and no slice is exploded or otherwise emphasized. The “Approximate Number Generation” pie shows 3 slices with internal labels and percentages: “Approximate Quantities” in a light beige/cream color at about 45.03%, “Comparative Relationships” in light blue at about 36.26%, and “Absolute Absence” in light lavender at about 18.71%; no legend or emphasis is present, and the slices appear arranged roughly from largest to smallest. The “Disjunctive & Conjunctive” pie shows 2 slices with internal labels and percentages: “Conjunctive” in pale mauve at about 50.49% and “Disjunctive” in very light blue at about 49.51%; no legend is included and neither slice is visually offset.
